q1_issues.issue: The degree hedge "so" is dropped entirely, so the parse states the flat denial "the zoo is not big" rather than the weaker hedged claim "not so big" (≈ not particularly big).

q2_gaps: Degree adverb under copular negation ("not **so** big", "not very big"): the Degree construction is stated for an asserted positive property (assert the positive ADJ plus `(Degree X <scale> <level>)`), and nothing says where the degree level goes when the property itself is denied at strength 0 — the Yet rule is the only precedent for keeping a modifier outside a strength-0 denial, and it is not generalized to Degree.
"so" as an intensifier is not among the listed surface levels (very / really / extremely / slightly / somewhat / fairly), so whether it is a recordable intensifier at all is unstated.
notes: The rest matches the instruction set exactly: definite "the zoo" as a typed witness, "in Prague" as the static `LocatedIn` (not an event oblique), the mandatory `(Name prague "Prague")`, and negation as strength 0.0 on the same atom with no QuantifierPhrase companion for plain "not".
